name: Survival
definition: Characters facing a hostile environment must manage finite resources, changing hazards, and social choices that reveal what remaining alive is for.
negative_signals: active human pursuer as the only danger
large-scale rescue logistics as the central focus
diagnostic_questions: Do material needs repeatedly shape character decisions?
Does adaptation matter more than simple endurance?

neighbors.distinction: Survival narrows attention to sustained adaptation; disaster foregrounds a large disruptive event and collective response.
Survival can lack an intentional adversary.

reader_promises.name: Material pressure
reader_promises.description: Make weather, injury, hunger, distance, or tools impose specific changing choices.

reader_promises.name: Reason to live
reader_promises.description: Connect physical endurance to relationships, values, guilt, or a future worth reaching.

roles.name: Adaptive survivor
roles.description: Learns from failure and converts limited knowledge into action.

roles.name: Companion
roles.description: Adds capability and a competing need, value, or pace.

roles.name: Distant aid
roles.description: Represents uncertain rescue, instruction, or false hope.

stakes: Return to or rejection of former life

movements.name: Stranding
movements.description: Remove ordinary support and define the first urgent need.

movements.name: Stabilization
movements.description: Secure temporary safety while revealing limits in knowledge or resources.

movements.name: Adaptation
movements.description: Turn learned environmental patterns into a difficult route or sustainable practice.

movements.name: Final survival choice
movements.description: Risk remaining resources for escape, rescue, community, or a chosen future.

complications.name: Resource loss
complications.description: A tool or supply fails because of prior use, environment, or error.

complications.name: Changing capability
complications.description: Injury or exhaustion redistributes tasks and acceptable risk.

complications.name: Environmental shift
complications.description: Weather, terrain, or ecology changes the viability of the current plan.

twists.name: Rescue is dangerous
twists.description: The apparent rescue route creates a credible greater threat or moral cost.

twists.name: Home unavailable
twists.description: Survival succeeds physically but returning to the former life is no longer possible.

conclusions.name: Rescued
conclusions.description: Aid arrives because characters made themselves reachable and endured the final cost.

conclusions.name: Self-extraction
conclusions.description: Survivors escape through accumulated knowledge and changed cooperation.

conclusions.name: New life
conclusions.description: Characters remain or relocate after redefining survival as more than return.

subversions: Let careful maintenance matter more than heroic exertion.
Make cooperation with the environment replace conquest of it.
cliches_to_avoid: Hazards that ignore established environmental rules
quality_checks: The ending answers both survival and its personal purpose.

sources.title: A Checklist for Critiquing Science Fiction
sources.author_or_organization: Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association
sources.contribution: Emphasizes consistent environments, motivated action, causality, stakes, and dramatic economy.

sources.title: The Narrative Arc: Revealing Core Narrative Structures through Text Analysis
sources.author_or_organization: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences / PMC
sources.contribution: Supports flexible internal narrative processes rather than one universal visible template.
